messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

The reports we have are all revision=1 (no later revisions). So they are all visible.

Then we keep only those events that have event_time <= target_time. target_time is 100. So we consider events with event_time<=100.

Then we apply those events in order of (event_time, event_id) from the starting initial_stock which is 16.

We need to compute: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions (i.e., lost sales from the events up to target_time). We also need to do a stock snapshot at horizon_time 130 including future schedule after the historical reconstruction. So after we have the reconstructed stock at target_time, we then apply every event in future_schedule in order (event_time, event_id) from the reconstructed stock up to horizon_time presumably (horizon_time is 130). The last event at time 129 is included (as time <= horizon_time). So we apply all future events.

We are to compute stock_at_horizon after the scenario (i.e., after applying all future_schedule events up to horizon_time). Also compute future_lost for the scenario only (i.e., lost sales that happen in future_schedule events after target_time). Also find first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if none. Only consider demands in future_schedule for stockout detection, not historical ones.

All of this should be returned as ints.

We also note that the system is lost-sales: demand consumes min(stock, quantity); any excess demand is lost, not backordered; that "lost" counts as lost sales.

Stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, i.e., lost >0 for a demand event; not simply stock ends at zero.

We should also note that receipts add quantity to stock (increase). There may be no negative receipts.

We also need to be careful about ordering: "Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order". Since event_id is a string, but we need to define alphabetical order? It is likely lexical order.
